content.text: Jira transitions can require screen fields (resolution, a mandatory comment, custom fields). gadak asks for them and throws them away.
- internal/jira/write.go:81-104 — Transitions() requests ?expand=transitions.fields, but the Transition struct has only ID/Name/To. The field metadata is parsed away.
- Transition() POSTs {"transition":{"id":...}} and nothing else. origin.Writer.Transition has no fields argument.

- gadak transition --help has no field flag. REST POST <key>/transition/ takes transition_id only (internal/server/write.go:468-479). The web path is the same (web/src/lib/api.ts:647). So CLI, REST and web all fail together.

- issuetap: GET /rest/api/3/issue/TAP-1/transitions?expand=transitions.fields returns no "fields" key at all. POST {"transition":{"id":"2"},"fields":{"resolution":{"id":"10002"}}} answers 204 and then stores resolution 10000/Done — the requested Duplicate(10002) is ignored (Store.Transition forces 10000 when the target is done).

Why it matters beyond the missing feature: on a workflow that requires a resolution, Cloud rejects the transition and standalone accepts it. An agent that learned the shape against issuetap ships code that breaks against Jira — the divergence class, not just a write gap.

- gadak: parse transitions.fields (required/schema/allowedValues); refuse before POST when a required field is unset, printing what is needed the way an unknown transition name already prints the available ones; carry fields through Writer, CLI (--resolution / --field alias=value / --comment), REST and web.

- issuetap: return a fields object on expand (empty is fine) and, when a fixture marks a transition field required, answer 400 when it is absent instead of silently succeeding. Not a workflow engine — just enough that standalone green cannot hide Cloud red. Stop hardcoding resolution 10000.

Gate: fake-Jira required-resolution transition POSTed without fields → 400 keyed on resolution; with fields → 2xx and the mirror's resolution matches the id sent. issuetap: expand response contains fields; required fixture without fields → 400; with fields → the given id is stored.
Found by the Jira-surface gap sweep (track C, score 10/10).
